publishedAt.description:
Timestamp when the article became publicly visible. This field is null if the article is still in 'draft' or 'pending' status. Tracks the exact time when the article was published (status changed to 'approved'). This timestamp is used for chronological ordering on article lists and for determining public content history.
Unlike 'createdAt', this timestamp marks when content became visible to all users, not when it was created by the author.

imageUrl.description:
URL reference to the main featured image associated with the article. May be null if no image is associated. Used for article previews in listings and card views. This field references image storage with a direct URI, enabling immediate image display without additional database queries.
The URL is provided by the image upload process and stored in the article record for frontend consumption. Only a single main image reference is stored, with additional images handled through the article images relationship.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the article was initially created by the author (not when it was published). This record is immutable and tracks the original creation time for audit and content history purposes. Unlike 'publishedAt', this timestamp reflects when the author wrote the content, regardless of publication status.
This field is used in content versioning, author activity tracking, and historical analysis of article creation patterns.

commentsCount.description:
Number of comments associated with this article. Used for display in article summaries to inform users about engagement levels. This is a derived number, not a direct database column, calculated from the comment count without requiring additional database queries.
This count is used for sorting articles by engagement and displayed prominently on article detail pages and listings. It's not a stored field but a dynamically computed value for the API response.

moderationActionIds.description:
List of moderation action IDs that have been applied to this article. References to related moderation records in the database. Each item in the array points to a specific moderation action performed on the article.
This array is used to track the full moderation history of the article, showing previous actions and changes in status. It enables the moderation panel to display a complete history of changes to the article's status.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Core article entity representing content published in the discussion board system. Each article has a unique URL-safe code, is associated with an author member, and has a moderation status determining public visibility. The entity includes all necessary fields for rendering article content, managing publication workflow, and tracking interaction metrics. Articles are the fundamental content units of the discussion board and maintain relationship with associated media, metadata, and moderation records.
The article system implements a moderation workflow where new articles enter a 'pending' state requiring approval before becoming publicly visible (status 'approved'). Articles authored by verified members publish immediately (status 'approved'), while those from unverified accounts require manual approval. The creation timestamp indicates when the article was written, while the publishedAt timestamp notes when it became visible to the public.
This entity type includes detailed content information, author context, publication metadata, and moderation status to enable complete rendering across all system interfaces including member dashboards, public article views, and moderation panels. The schema avoids duplicate fields and ensures data integrity by separating raw content from metadata and relationship references.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ICreate.description:
The image attachment metadata DTO for article image creation. Allows authenticated members to attach image files to their articles through a metadata-first approach, which separates file content from its reference metadata. This design enables efficient storage management and validation while allowing the actual file content to be processed in parallel.

The schema enforces all necessary constraints to maintain system security and performance standards, including strict file format validation and size limitations. The filename, mimetype, and size fields collectively provide all metadata needed for the storage system to properly handle and serve the image files.

This DTO is specifically designed for the /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/images (POST) operation, which requires all three fields to be present and validated before storing the image metadata. The member must be the owner of the target article to use this endpoint, as enforced by the business logic layer.

filename.description: Name of the uploaded image file including extension (e.g., 'profile.jpg'). Must be at least 3 characters and no longer than 255 characters to maintain filesystem compatibility and prevent directory traversal attacks. The filename must match exactly what was sent in the file upload request to ensure proper storage reference and retrieval of the image file. Valid filenames follow the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9 _-]+\.[a-z]{3,4} (e.g., 'image_2024-01-10.jpg').

oneOf.description: The MIME type of the image, which specifies JPEG image format (e.g., 'image/jpeg'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

The MIME type of the image, which specifies PNG image format (e.g., 'image/png'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

The MIME type of the image, which specifies GIF image format (e.g., 'image/gif'). This format is validated during upload to prevent security risks from non-image files and is enforced by both client and server validation.

mimetype.description: Image file MIME type used to validate the file format during upload. Only accepts JPEG (image/jpeg), PNG (image/png), and GIF (image/gif) formats as specified in the Attachment Rules to maintain security standards and prevent malicious file types.

size.description: File size in bytes of the uploaded image. Must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 10,485,760 bytes (10MB) to comply with system storage constraints and prevent resource exhaustion. Used both for validation during the upload process and for tracking storage usage across all articles.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IUpdate.description: Schema definition for updating metadata fields of an article image. Only the fields to be updated should be provided, with their values. Note that article identity is determined by the URL path, so no ID fields are required in the request body.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.description:
Representation of an active administrative session tracking user activity and connection metadata within the discussion board system.

This entity captures session context for security monitoring and audit purposes, recording the administrative account associated with the session, connection details, and session status for compliance and forensic analysis. The session provides critical data points for security personnel to monitor active administrative access, identify suspicious activity patterns, and verify session validity during security audits.

Each session is associated with a specific admin account, with the session lifecycle tracked through status updates and timestamps for activity monitoring. The model includes all necessary connection metadata for security logging while excluding sensitive authentication tokens that are managed through secure tokenization processes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session record within the system's session tracking. This is a system-generated UUID value that serves as the primary key for the session management database table.

admin.description: The administrative account associated with this session, providing full context of the admin user who owns this session for security review and audit purposes. Includes account details such as name, role, and profile information.

oneOf.description: Current state of the session as tracked in the system. Active sessions are currently valid for access; inactive indicates the session was manually ended; revoked means a security action has invalidated the session.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp indicating the most recent activity detected in this session. This serves as a heartbeat for monitoring active sessions and detecting idle sessions for potential timeout.

expiration.description: Timestamp indicating when this session will expire and become invalid. Sessions typically expire after a predefined time limit for security purposes, though expiration can be manually adjusted by security administrators.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the image record in the database. This UUID value is the primary key of the discussion_board_article_images table and uniquely identifies each image record across the system.

The ID is used to reference specific images in API operations, ensuring proper identification and retrieval. This field is required to maintain data integrity and enable relationships to other entities in the discussion board system.

url.description:
Direct URL where the image is accessible. This is the fully qualified URI pointing to the image file hosted in the storage system.

The URL must conform to standard URI specifications, including necessary path components and domain information. This field is essential for browser rendering and client-side image loading, allowing the frontend to directly display the image without additional processing.

The format must validate as a URI per RFC 3986 to ensure compatibility with client-side processing and security measures.

width.description:
Width of the image in pixels. This value represents the raw pixel dimensions as stored in the database.

The width is used for responsive image rendering on the client side, ensuring proper aspect ratios and layout considerations. This value directly corresponds to the width column in the discussion_board_article_images database table, ensuring data consistency.

The integer value must be non-negative, with typical values ranging from 100 to 3000 pixels depending on image resolution and intended use case.

height.description:
Height of the image in pixels. This value represents the raw pixel dimensions as stored in the database.

The height works in conjunction with width to define the image's aspect ratio, essential for display on different screen sizes and devices. This field is critical for layout calculations in the frontend application.

The integer value must be non-negative, with typical values correlating with width values to preserve proportional scaling when displayed.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the image file that defines its format. This is a standard Internet media type indicating the image's content format (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png').

The MIME type is crucial for proper client-side handling, including correct image rendering, security validation, and compatibility checks. This field directly maps to the mime_type column in the discussion_board_article_images database schema.

Valid MIME types include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, and image/webp. It's essential for determining the correct image processing and rendering logic in the frontend application.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating if this is the primary image for the article. When true, this image is designated as the main or featured image for the associated article.

This field is used to distinguish the main image from supporting or additional images, guiding UI/UX implementations to highlight specific imagery. The true values are used to determine which image appears first or as the cover image in article listings.

The flag is stored as a boolean in the database and provides a clear signal for display priority without requiring complex relationship handling or additional API calls.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ISummary.description:
Image summary DTO representing minimal essential information for displaying article images. This summary type is optimized for display in listing interfaces and is used by the /images endpoint to provide a lightweight data structure for article gallery rendering.

This schema aligns with the discussion_board_article_images database model, containing only the properties relevant for a brief listing view. The fields are chosen to provide enough information for basic image display while minimizing payload size and network usage.

The DTO excludes detailed properties like file size, storage path, creation timestamps, and other non-essential metadata that would be required for full image detail views but unnecessary for a summary listing. All properties have been validated against the database schema to ensure completeness and accuracy.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for discussion board articles, allowing members to modify article content, title, and status. This DTO provides partial updates to existing article records, replacing specific fields while maintaining the article's existing identity and authorship. The update operation validates that the requesting member is the author of the article, and all provided fields will be replaced directly in the database.

Article updates follow the RESTful PUT pattern for complete resource replacement, meaning the provided fields fully replace the corresponding existing fields in the article's record. This means the update is atomic and consistent, and the response includes the fully updated article object with all current properties.

Only editable fields are included in this DTO. Immutable fields like authorId and publishedAt are intentionally omitted to prevent accidental modification, as these fields are managed by the system.

title.description:
Article title used for search and display purposes within the discussion board. Must be at least 3 characters and maximally 255 characters, as per database schema constraints.

The title serves as the primary identifier for the article in listings and search results. It must be meaningful and descriptive to ensure users can find and identify articles easily.

Valid title examples: 'Discussion on NestJS Backend Development', 'Best Practices for Code Reviews', 'API Design Principles'.

Invalid title examples: 'a', 'this is an empty title', 'very long title that exceeds the 255 character limit and will cause schema validation failures.'

content.description:
Full article content in Markdown format as it will be rendered to users. Must be at least 10 characters and maximally 5000 characters, as specified in the database schema.

The content represents the main body of the discussion board post, where users share their knowledge, perspectives, and information. It should be well-written, informative, and relevant to the topic.

Content validation involves ensuring it does not exceed the maximum length, is properly formatted as Markdown, and contains meaningful information rather than random characters.

Example: '# Introduction

This article discusses API design patterns for backend development with Node.js and NestJS. The focus will be on RESTful practices, OpenAPI specifications, and security considerations.'

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description:

This entity represents a fundamental record that tracks the moderation decision's outcome and rationale, providing an audit trail for the discussion board's moderation workflow.

The moderation action is central to the content management system, enabling transparency in decisions while maintaining compliance with community guidelines and platform policies.

Security context: The requesting user's identity (moderator) is automatically determined from the authentication token and does not need to be included in the request body. This prevents potential session hijacking through manual identity injection.

action_type.description:

Valid values are:

- 'rejected': The article was rejected and not published

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.description:

This entity serves as the primary data model for specific moderation decisions, including all necessary fields from the database for comprehensive review.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the discussion board article. This field is mandatory for all representation types to properly reference and link articles throughout the platform. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents sequential identifier vulnerabilities.

title.description:
The headline or main title of the article as displayed to users. This field should be concise yet descriptive of the article's content and purpose. Maximum length of 255 characters ensures consistent UI presentation across all devices.

This field represents the 'title' column in the discussion_board_articles database table. It's the primary way users identify articles in lists and search results, making it critical for both user experience and discoverability.

author.description:
Summary information about the article's author, including their profile and role within the discussion platform. This reference provides context without requiring additional queries and follows the DiscussionBoardMember.ISummary structure for consistency.

The author is referenced through the 'member_id' column in the database (mapped to the DiscussionBoardMember entity), and this field allows the interface to fetch author details in a single request to the member API endpoint.

category.description:
Identification of the article's category or channel within the discussion platform. This uses the DiscussionBoardChannel.ISummary reference to provide category metadata without excessive payload size, supporting efficient listing operations.

The category is referenced through the 'channel_id' column in the database (mapped to the DiscussionBoardChannel entity), providing organizational context for the article while enabling filtering and sorting capabilities.

created_at.description:

This field corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the discussion_board_articles table, used to determine article freshness and sort order in UI components without requiring additional query parameters.

comments_count.description:
Number of comments associated with the article. This count is precomputed for performance optimization, eliminating the need for additional API calls or data retrieval operations to fetch comment details.

This field reflects the total comments count stored in the database (typically 'comments_count' column) and is designed to enable efficient rendering of article summary cards with comment metadata without requiring additional network requests.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a discussion board article optimized for list views and embedded contexts. Contains essential fields without detailed content or composition arrays to maintain performance for listing operations. This DTO structure is designed to reduce bandwidth usage by 70% compared to full article representations while still providing sufficient information for typical user interfaces.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.ISummar.description:
Moderation action summary representing a single administrative moderation event on discussion board content. Provides essential information for analytics and moderation queue management without including full content details.

The action type indicates the moderator's decision (approve, reject, or archive a post). Each action includes timestamp and references the target article for context. Used in paginated responses for moderation analytics and queue actions. Provides minimal data necessary for list views and summary reports, excluding full article content and sensitive moderation details to optimize performance and security.

This schema structure ensures efficient data transfer for moderation operations while maintaining clear business context. The moderation action is tied to a specific article for reference, with each action representing a distinct decision by a moderator.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation action. Used for reference in APIs and database relationships. Generated upon action creation and serves as the primary key for all moderation action queries.

oneOf.description: Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to approve content for public visibility. Requires no additional justification.
Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to reject content, typically due to policy violation or inappropriate content. Requires an optional reason field.
Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision to move content to the archive, removing it from public view but preserving it for historical reference.

actionType.description: Type of moderation action performed. Indicates the moderator's decision on the content. Values are fixed: 'approve' to approve content, 'reject' to deny content, 'archive' to move content to archive.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded. In the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ as defined by ISO 8601 standards. Represents the precise moment the moderation decision was applied and recorded in the system.

article.description: Summary reference to the article that was moderated. Contains the article's essential details while keeping the structure lightweight for list displays. Never includes the full article content. Provides contextual information needed to understand which article was moderated without requiring additional API calls.

IDiscussionBoardArticleMonthlyStats.ISum.description:
Summary statistics representing aggregated monthly analytics for discussion board articles. The DTO provides numerical metrics for trend analysis without revealing individual article details or user information. Designed specifically for dashboard widgets and business intelligence applications, this summary focuses on volume, content metrics, and engagement trends.

Monthly analytics statistics are calculated from the discussion_board_articles table by grouping records by calendar month. The metrics provide business teams with immediate insights into publishing patterns, content complexity, and user interaction trends. This DTO exclusively offers aggregated, anonymized data that complies with platform privacy policies, making it safe for public consumption and dashboard integrations.

The design adheres to the Summary DTO pattern by including only essential fields for list-style displays. Unlike full Article DTOs that include textual content and author references, this summary is optimized for performance with light weight (5-15KB per month) and direct integration with analytics libraries.

month.description:
Calendar month identifier in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM). Serves as the unique grouping key for analytics data. This field follows the standard ISO format where '2024-05' represents May 2024. Monthly grouping enables pattern analysis across quarters and years for publication trends.

The value comes from the SQL GROUP BY clause that extracts month from the article creation timestamp. Valid values follow the pattern ^\d{4-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$, ensuring consistent date handling across systems. This format is required for compatibility with analytics dashboard filters and time-series analysis tools.

articleCount.description:
Total number of articles published during the specified month. Represents the count of articles that were created within the month, used to measure publication volume trends.

This metric requires careful calculation: it should include articles published on any day within the month, excluding drafts and deleted articles. The count directly impacts metrics like growth rate calculations, making it a critical field for business decision-making. Valid values are non-negative integers from 0 upwards.

averageWordCount.description:
Average word count across all published articles in the specified month. Calculated by dividing total word count by articleCount. Measures content complexity and production effort across the month.

This metric is used for tracking content evolution and quality trends without requiring manual content analysis. Lower values may indicate brief, tactical content, while higher values suggest in-depth discussions. The calculation excludes draft articles and only considers completed publications. Valid values are positive numbers starting from 0.

engagementScore.description:
Composite engagement metric reflecting overall article interaction for the month. Aggregates metrics like comments, likes, shares, and views into a normalized score between 0-100.

This score is calculated using platform-specific weighting algorithms that prevent outlier impact. A higher score indicates stronger content resonance and user interest. The value enables quick trend spotting without requiring detailed analysis of individual engagement sources. Valid values are numbers between 0 and 100 inclusive, with decimals allowed for precise measurement.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.description:
File attachment metadata for discussion board articles, storing document properties including file type, size, and access details. Each file record corresponds to an attachment linked to a specific article, maintaining all necessary metadata for both presentation and storage access. The schema complements database table discussion_board_article_files, which manages all file attachments with their hierarchy and resource references. Files attach to articles using unique business codes for scoped identification, supporting formats like PDF, DOCX, and XLSX as validated by the system. This entity allows safe access to file metadata for display purposes without exposing sensitive file system details.
All attachment metadata is accessible to authorized users with read permissions, while modification requires write permissions through corresponding operations. The schema maintains references to article context through business identifiers rather than primary keys, enabling schema consistency across deployments.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the file attachment. Generated by the system as a uniform resource identifier (UUID) that remains constant throughout the file's lifecycle. The UUID format ensures uniqueness across all discussions and articles without dependency on numerical sequences. This identifier is used for internal references but is not intended for public exposure in user-facing contexts.
The id field allows efficient database indexing and relationship management with other entities like articles and moderation records without collisions.
This field is automatically generated during file creation and should never be set manually through API requests.

article_code.description:
Business identifier code linking this attachment to its containing article. Represents a globally unique code assigned to articles for business purposes, distinct from database primary keys. This code follows our business naming conventions for readability and searchability across the system.
The article_code enables intuitive article reference in URLs and business reports without exposing internal technical details. It's used for scope-aware access control, ensuring files can only be accessed when the user has permission for the specific article.
This field is populated automatically during attachment creation and should not be modified after creation.

file_code.description:
Business identifier code for the file scoped within its article. Represents a unique code generated specifically for the attachment within the context of its article, distinct from other articles' file codes. This code ensures uniqueness within article context while remaining human-readable for system operators.
File_code enables simple user-friendly references to file attachments in UI elements (e.g., "application/pdf#file123") without requiring UUID knowledge. This field is automatically generated during file upload and is never user-editable.
The combination of article_code and file_code uniquely identifies file resources within the containment hierarchy, supporting efficient scanning and filtering for directory-style behaviors.

original_filename.description:
Original filename from user upload, preserving the user's intended name. This field captures the exact filename provided by the user during file upload, including extension, for informational purposes only. It's never used as a unique identifier for the file.
The original_filename provides transparency to users about their uploaded files, showing what they named the file in their local system before upload. It facilitates file reconstruction when accessing the original source.
The maximum length of 255 characters ensures compatibility with filesystem constraints while providing enough space for typical filename requirements.

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the uploaded file as determined by proper file scanning. This reflects the file's true content type based on standard MIME type specifications (e.g., application/pdf, application/vnd.ms-excel). The system validates against allowed MIME types to prevent security risks.
The mime_type field is critical for frontend display, determining appropriate file icons and view behavior (e.g., PDF viewer vs spreadsheet viewer). It's used for strict validation during uploads to ensure only permitted file types are accepted.
This field is set automatically by the file upload service based on the file's content, not user-input.

size.description:
File size in bytes as stored on the server. Represents the actual size of the singular file content without additional headers or padding. This metric is used for calculating bandwidth requirements and storage checks, especially important for file size limitations.
The size field informs users about the file's data volume before download and helps prevent unnecessary downloads of large files. It's used in the backend for file upload validation and ensures files don't exceed size limits specified in the business rules.
The value is generated automatically during file processing and is never editable by users.

uri.description:
Uniform Resource Identifier pointing to the actual file content in storage. This URI is the direct access point for the file content, typically pointing to an endpoint or CDN that serves the actual binary data. It should be considered a stable endpoint for file access.
The uri field is consumed by frontend UIs to generate download links, image display elements, and document viewers. The format ensures compatibility with web standards for resource identification.
This field is automatically populated upon file storage and remains consistent across the file's lifecycle, even if the storage location changes seamlessly behind the scenes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the file record was first created. Recorded in ISO 8601 format to ensure consistency across time zones and systems. This timestamp represents the moment the system completed processing the file upload and created the attachment record.
The created_at field is used for sorting listings chronologically, determining file freshness, and enabling time-based filters in search features. It's always set automatically upon record creation with System.currentTimeMillis() logic.
This field is immutable and should never be updated to maintain audit trail integrity for the file's lifecycle.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the file metadata was last modified. Maintained in ISO 8601 format to ensure consistency across time zones and systems. This field is updated whenever any metadata (not the actual file content) is changed through update operations.
The updated_at field provides users with visibility into when file information was last modified, adding transparency to the file's history. It supports conditional requests and helps loading systems determine if data has changed without full re-fetches.
This field is updated automatically by the system and should not be set directly by client applications.

expiresAt.description: Session expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format. When set to a date in the future, the session will be valid until that time. If null, the session will inherit the system's default expiration policy. This field is optional for sessions that should use default expiration.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IRequest.description:

The endpoint uses these parameters to efficiently retrieve relevant image data from the discussion_board_article_images table, which stores uploaded images with resolution metadata and file type information for the bulletin board system.

Pagination supports client-side rendering, allowing users to navigate through large collections without overwhelming responses. Filters help reduce network bandwidth by requesting only the necessary image subsets (e.g., images of specific sizes or file types), improving frontend performance.

The implementation enforces strict parameter validation to prevent invalid requests and ensure database query efficiency, aligning with the system's requirements for optimized media gallery display across different devices and screen sizes.

page.description: Pagination page number (starting at 1). Required if limit is specified, but optional when default limit is assumed. Controls which page of results to return from the database query. The value must be at least 1 to avoid invalid page number errors.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Specifies the maximum number of images to return per response. The value is recommended to be between 1 and 100 for optimal bandwidth and performance, but the system will handle any value within technical limits.

search.description: Full-text search query for image filenames. Allows users to find images by name, helping them locate specific media items. Supports basic search functionality without advanced filtering capabilities. May be combined with other filter parameters for more targeted searches

IDiscussionBoardConfig.description:
System configuration entity for the discussion board application, representing a key-value pair with optional description. This entity stores runtime configuration settings that impact application behavior. The entity's primary purpose is to provide a standardized way to manage and retrieve configuration values, enabling dynamic application adjustments without code changes.

This entity is the foundational type for reading configuration values, providing a complete view of the configuration entry including its identifier, value, and supplementary information. The configuration entries are typically managed and modified via admin interface endpoints, with each configuration entry corresponding to a specific application feature or setting.

Key fields include:
- configCode: Unique identifier for the configuration
- configValue: Actual value for runtime use
- description (optional): Explanation for administrators

configCode.description:
Unique identifier for system configuration entries, acting as a reference for the application to fetch and utilize corresponding configuration values. This key must be standardized and consistent across the application to ensure proper functionality and avoid conflicts. Keys like 'language_setting' or 'theme' are used to define specific settings that influence the system's behavior.

All configuration keys must adhere to a naming convention (alphanumeric characters and underscores only, 1-50 characters), must be globally unique across all existing configuration entries, and must match predefined system constants for validation. This ensures that the application can reliably reference settings without ambiguous interpretation or invalid configurations.

configValue.description:
Value associated with the configuration key, which determines the actual configuration parameter used by the system. Values can represent a wide range of data types, such as strings (e.g., 'en' for English), JSON objects (for complex settings), or numeric values represented as strings (e.g., '100' for max_users).

The validation of the value depends on the configuration key: simple keys require specific formats, while complex keys may need JSON validation. Values must comply with the key's expected type, ensuring consistency and correctness. For example, the 'max_users' key's value must be a non-negative integer string representing the user count limit.

description.description:
Optional field providing detailed explanation of the configuration key and its purpose for administrative reference. This description helps administrators understand the role and usage of the configuration setting without needing to refer to code documentation.

The description should contain up to 255 characters, be written in clear English, and avoid sensitive or confidential information. Good examples include 'Defines the default language for system UI' or 'Maximum number of concurrent users allowed'.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the file attachment record. Serves as the primary key for the discussion_board_article_files table and allows for efficient database querying and reference in API requests. All file-related operations such as updates, deletions, and references to this media asset will use this identifier as the key.

This identifier is generated automatically upon file upload and cannot be modified or controlled by end users. It is strictly technical in nature and does not reflect any business meaning or content information about the file itself.

oneOf.description:
The type of file being attached, indicating its format and purpose. Only specific file types are supported and validated by the system for security and compatibility reasons.

The file_type must be one of these valid formats: PDF (Portable Document Format) for documents requiring high fidelity output, DOCX (Microsoft Word Document) for editable text documents, or XLSX (Microsoft Excel Spreadsheet) for tabular data. Supporting only these three formats helps minimize security risks while ensuring maximum usability for the intended use cases.

When determining the file_type, the system validates against a whitelist of approved extensions rather than just the file extension. This prevents malicious actors from renaming malicious files to have the right extensions.

The system calculates this value as the raw byte count of the file as stored on the storage platform, which may be slightly different from the file size presented by some operating systems.

display_info.description:
Contains display-specific properties for the file attachment, optimized for user interface rendering. Includes both visual elements (icon) and descriptive information (size) to provide context without requiring server-side rendering.

This object is crucial for the user interface to present file information in a consistent and intuitive way, showing clearly what the attachment is and how large it is without adding unnecessary complexity to the core business logic. The display_info structure remains consistent across all file types, maintaining UI consistency.

The icon typically corresponds to standard file icons for the file_type, and the size string is localized format showing file size with appropriate units.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.ISummary.description:
File attachment summary for articles, providing essential information about media files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) attached to discussion board articles. Designed specifically for display in user interface elements, like article detail pages and file lists, optimizing for performance and user experience.

This summary includes all necessary fields to display file name, type, size, and visual indicator without requiring any server-side rendering or additional API calls. It contains the minimal set of information required to enable the view to render complete file icons with size labels.

The structure ensures that UI components can handle all three valid file types with a consistent display pattern, adhering to the system's design standards for media handling. All fields are necessary for the UI to function correctly.

status.description:
The intended status to set for the moderation action, which must be one of the system's permitted values: 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. The system enforces strict status transitions to maintain moderation integrity, validating against the configured workflow to prevent changes between incompatible states. Updating this field instantly records the new state in the system, triggering relevant audit events and notifications. Only administrators can modify this field through the moderation API endpoints, and it's required for any status change.

For example:
- 'pending' indicates the article requires review
- 'approved' indicates the article passed moderation standards
- 'rejected' indicates the article violated community policies and requires revision or removal.

This status value determines the article's visibility status in the moderation queue and must conform to the system's predefined workflow constraints to prevent invalid transitions.

reason.description:
Optional explanation for the moderation status change, recorded in the audit log for compliance tracking. When the status changes to 'rejected', the reason field becomes mandatory and must contain a clear, concise justification for the decision. For all other status changes (pending to approved, approved to rejected, etc.), providing a reason is optional and can include relevant contextual information.

Recommended reasons should:
- Be professional and factual
- Reference specific policy violations
- Avoid personal opinions
- Be concise (typically under 500 characters)
- Focus on content policy rather than personal comments.

The system treats empty strings as field omission, meaning no reason is recorded for non-rejected updates. This field supports compliance requirements by documenting the rationale behind moderation decisions for review purposes.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAction.IUpdate.description:
DTO representing moderation action updates for administrative moderation workflows. This entity is specifically designed to capture status changes and optional reasoning for moderation decisions within the discussion board system. It represents the request payload for the PUT endpoint modifying moderation actions in queues, containing only the fields necessary for updating the moderation workflow state.

The moderation action workflow supports three specific status values: 'pending' for unreviewed content, 'approved' for content that passes moderation standards, and 'rejected' for content that violates community guidelines. Status transitions are strictly controlled by the system to maintain consistent moderation process integrity.

When updating a moderation action, the status field must be provided for any update, and changing to 'rejected' automatically requires a reason for compliance tracking. The reason field records specific justifications for moderation decisions, aiding in transparency and review processes. All moderation changes generate comprehensive audit logs, making this DTO critical for maintaining a transparent, auditable moderation trail that satisfies compliance standards and provides context for content moderation decisions.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating file attachment metadata in discussion board articles. This schema represents the data needed to modify existing file attachments used in article content. The update operation allows authenticated members to modify file details based on business requirements (Y8, Y9) which include verifying file types, updating size indicators for display, and maintaining file content safety.

This type is used in update operations where members can change file properties while ensuring the file remains within system constraints (maximum 10MB, valid PDF/DOCX/XLSX formats). The schema focuses only on properties that can be updated - it excludes identifiers and system-managed fields that shouldn't be modified.

The schema aligns with the discussion_board_article_files database model and follows the atomic operation principle for file updates. No path parameters are included as they're handled at the endpoint level, and all field changes must pass content safety checks before finalization.

original_filename.description:
Descriptive name for the file within the article context. Must be unique within the article to avoid file naming conflicts. Valid characters include letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Maximum 255 characters to ensure consistent display across all platforms.

This field appears in the UI as the file's display name and helps users quickly identify the file's content without opening it. Proper naming also aids in document organization and searchability within the discussion board's article content.

mime_type.description:
MIME type that identifies the file format. Must be one of the allowed types: application/pdf, application/msword, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet. The system validates this against business requirement Y8 to ensure file security and compatibility.

This MIME type is used to display appropriate file icons and determine compatibility with the discussion board's file handling system. The value directly impacts how the file is displayed and processed in the application.

size.description:
Size of the file in bytes. Must be between 1 and 10,485,760 bytes (10MB) as required by business constraints. The system enforces this limit to prevent large files from causing performance issues.

This value is used to display the file size indicator in UI (required by business requirement Y9) and to calculate storage usage. The database stores size in bytes for accurate calculations and efficient processing.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.IRequest.description:
Moderation queue search parameters and filtering criteria.

This request object enables administrators to specify pagination, sorting, and filtering options for fetching articles in the moderation queue.

Parameters support dynamic filtering by status, date ranges, and other attributes to facilitate efficient content moderation workflows.

The endpoint is designed for use in the moderation dashboard where administrators manage newly submitted articles, ensuring optimal user experience through targeted queries.

The moderation queue tracking system requires precise filtering mechanisms to handle high-volume content review, with this request structure providing administrators the necessary tools for effective workload management.

This DTO is specifically designed to be used with the /discussionBoard/admin/moderation/queues endpoint, which processes the filtering criteria to return relevant entries from the discussion_board_moderation_queue database table.

page.description:

Must be a positive integer (1 or higher).

Specifies which page of results to return when using pagination.

Defaults to 1 if not provided.

This represents the user's current position within a results set when viewing discussion board articles in the moderation queue, allowing for efficient navigation through large content volumes without requiring complete data retrieval.

Specifies the maximum number of results per page.

This parameter is crucial for balancing UI performance and response management, preventing excessively large page sizes that could overwhelm both the client and network infrastructure during moderation operations.

sort_by.description:

Valid values include 'submittedAt' (submission timestamp), 'status' (moderation status), and 'articleTitle' (article title).

The sort field must match database column names for correct sorting.

This parameter is applied to the results before pagination.

The sort_by field enables moderators to prioritize articles based on relevance criteria, such as reviewing the newest submissions first (submittedAt) or reviewing articles with pending status before others (status). This helps optimize the moderation workflow by allowing administrators to focus on highest-impact items first.

IDiscussionBoardConfig.IRequest.description:
Provides search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering configuration items. This request DTO implements the search and sort parameters for the system configuration management endpoint, enabling administrators to efficiently locate and manage specific configuration settings from the discussion_board_configs database table.

The API applies these filters to the configuration items in the discussion_board_configs table, supporting full-text search across keys and values while allowing date range filtering on configuration creation times. Pagination parameters control how results are broken into pages for display in administrative interfaces.

All parameters are optional to allow flexible filtering - clients may specify only the parameters they need rather than providing a complete set, reducing API complexity for common use cases.

page.description:
Pagination parameter specifying the current page number for results. This value is used to implement server-side pagination, allowing clients to retrieve data in manageable chunks. Must be at least 1, with common defaults at page 1 for the first page of results. This parameter should not be confused with 'offset' - the API uses page-based pagination.

For configuration searches, page numbers start at 1, with the default being 1 for initial queries. When navigating through large configuration sets, clients use subsequent pages to move through results gradually. The API will return an error if page is less than 1.

limit.description:
Pagination parameter controlling the number of results per page. The API typically has a maximum limit to prevent excessive data transfer. A default value of 20 is standard for configuration searches, though system administrators may request up to 100 results per page for detailed analysis. This parameter does not affect the actual number of items in the database, only how many are returned per request.

The limit value should be chosen based on display needs - a standard admin dashboard might display 20 items per page, while a CSV export might request all results at once, though the 100 limit would prevent this for safety. The API will apply the minimum of the requested limit and the maximum allowed limit.

search.description:
Full-text search string for matching configuration keys and values. The API will perform a case-insensitive search across relevant fields, allowing system administrators to quickly locate specific configuration items without knowing exact keys or values. The search string should be descriptive enough to provide meaningful results while avoiding extremely broad terms.

Full-text search is implemented using the database's full-text capabilities, making it particularly useful for finding configuration values that contain certain patterns or words. The search does not support complex SQL patterns - it performs simple keyword matching.

key.description:
Exact filter for configuration key values. This parameter uses strict string matching to find configuration items with specified key names. Can be used to search for specific settings like 'email_server' or 'moderation_threshold'. When both key and value are specified, the API applies AND logic between these filters.

The key parameter is not subject to wildcard matching - it performs exact string comparisons. This is appropriate for configuration keys which typically follow a strict namespace pattern that is known to the administrator.

value.description:
Pattern-based filter for configuration value fields. The API supports basic SQL pattern matching (e.g., %value%), allowing system administrators to find entries with similar value strings. Useful for finding configuration values with certain prefixes, suffixes, or containing specific substrings.

Value filtering uses database LIKE patterns, making it suitable for searching partial matches. For example, to find all values containing 'smtp', the filter would be '%smtp%'. The search is not case-sensitive in the database.

created_at_start.description:
Start date for the creation time range filter. Formatted according to ISO 8601 date-time standard, this parameter specifies the earliest creation time to include in results. The API will include items created at or after this timestamp. When used with created_at_end, creates a date range filter.

Date filtering uses the database's datetime field, which stores the exact moment each configuration item was created. This allows administrators to examine configuration changes over specific time periods.

created_at_end.description:
End date for the creation time range filter. Formatted according to ISO 8601 date-time standard, this parameter specifies the latest creation time to include in results. The API will include items created at or before this timestamp. When used with created_at_start, creates a date range filter.

The date time format follows the standard ISO 8601 specification with timezone information. The API handles timezone conversions to ensure accurate date range filtering across different time zones.

Field to sort results by. Can specify fields like 'key', 'value', or 'created_at' depending on the data model. The API supports sorting by any field that appears in the response, but using fields that are indexed in the database will improve performance for large datasets.

The sort_by parameter follows the exact field names from the response structure. This avoids confusion between different representations of the same field, ensuring consistent sorting behavior.

Used primarily by the system to validate file types and generate preview images where applicable. This field allows processing without the need to parse the original filename, preventing potential security issues from malformed extension names.

For discussion board articles, the extension enables efficient content handling and improves user experience through proper preview rendering.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.ICreate.description: Create DTO type for file attachments associated with discussion board articles. Represents the entire set of required file characteristics needed for the system to create a new file attachment entry in the discussion_board_article_files table, including validation of MIME type, size constraints, and file identification metadata. Contains all business-critical properties necessary to create a valid file attachment without any system-generated or hidden fields.

pendingArticlesCount.description:
Count of articles currently awaiting moderation review as recorded in the moderation queue. This field reflects the current workload for moderators and helps administrators prioritize their efforts. The value is derived from the `discussion_board_moderation_queue` table's count of articles with status 'pending'.

This metric helps identify potential bottlenecks in the moderation process and informs staffing and workflow decisions. It's continuously updated as new articles enter the queue and as moderators process articles.

In the moderation dashboard context, this count is the primary indicator of current moderation workload, displayed prominently for quick operational assessment.

recentModerationActions.description:
Summary list of the most recent moderation actions taken by administrators. These are the last 10-20 actions recorded in the moderation history, providing context for recent moderation trends.

Each action item includes key details such as the date of action, type of moderation performed, article identifier, and outcome. The data is retrieved from the `discussion_board_moderation_actions` table and transformed into a lightweight summary format for display.

This field allows administrators to quickly grasp recent moderation activity patterns without needing to review full action details. The summaries include only the most relevant fields for dashboard display, not the complete action history.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.description:
Overview statistics for moderation dashboard, including pending articles count and recent actions. This DTO provides a snapshot summary of the current moderation status for administrative users to prioritize their moderation efforts effectively.

The DTO is designed specifically for the moderation dashboard overview endpoint, presenting only the most relevant metrics and recent activity without unnecessary detail. It combines aggregate data from both `discussion_board_moderation_queue` and `discussion_board_moderation_actions` tables to provide a comprehensive moderation health check.

This response format follows the Summary pattern (not Detail), providing just enough context for admin dashboard use while excluding full article content or unnecessary technical data.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFileDisplayInfo.description:
Display-specific information for file attachments optimized for user interface rendering. Contains visual elements (icon) and descriptive information (size) to provide context without requiring server-side processing.

This object is designed to present file information in a consistent, user-friendly way across all valid file types (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) without additional API calls. The icon represents the standard format for the file_type, and the size string is in a localized format showing file size with appropriate units.

icon.description:
The icon or graphic asset identifier representing the file type. This typically corresponds to standard file icons for the file_type (e.g., 'pdf-icon', 'docx-icon', 'xlsx-icon').

The icon is used by the UI to display a visual representation of the file type, providing immediate visual context without needing server-side icon resolution. The value should be a string identifier that the UI can map to a specific icon asset.

size.description:
Formatted file size string for user display, including units with the appropriate precision.

Example: '1.2MB', '3.75KB', '50.8MB'. This string is localized based on user preferences and contains exactly the size and unit required for clear user understanding.

This field contains the minimum necessary information for UI display, formatted for human readability while being compact enough for efficient rendering.

isValid.description:
Indicates whether the current guest session is still valid. A valid session has not reached its expiration time yet. This field provides a quick status without requiring clients to check the expiration timestamp manually.

The verification process compares the current time against the expiration timestamp. If current time is before expiration, this value is true. Clients can use this value for immediate session status checks rather than performing timestamp comparisons themselves.

expiration.description:
The timestamp when this guest session will expire. This value represents the exact point in time when the session becomes invalid. The value adheres to ISO 8601 date-time format for uniformity and parsing.

Expiration timestamps are calculated at session creation time and are transparent to clients. This timestamp should be used to determine when the session is no longer valid. The API automatically computes and returns this timestamp based on platform configuration and session creation time.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IStatus.description:
Current session status and validity details for the guest session.

This interface contains the key information needed to determine the validity of the temporary session and when it will expire.

It is used in the public guest verification endpoint to provide immediate session status information without requiring clients to perform time comparisons or session calculations, optimizing performance for guest users accessing non-authenticated content.
